topic: multi-provider gateways for local agent and CLI routing
research_method: Exa official-source search plus read-only fetch of immutable GitHub refs and official docs
scope: CLIProxyAPI, LiteLLM, Bifrost; no install, runtime execution, or local CLI configuration changes

items.summary: Latest stable release is v7.3.16, published 2026-09-24T00:10:28Z.
items.purpose: Fix the version/date anchor used for source inspection.
supports: CLIProxyAPI v7.3.16 is a current stable release at access time
items.boundary: Release metadata does not prove every README feature or runtime behavior.

items.summary: Tag v7.3.16 dereferences to commit c404af96ebacedf8168b3c2bdbf4449a21cd1c1e.
items.purpose: Pin immutable README/source URLs.
supports: fixed source revision for CLIProxyAPI evidence
items.boundary: Tag metadata says nothing about deployment or account safety.

items.summary: CLI-focused OpenAI/Gemini/Claude/Codex/Grok compatible proxy; lists OAuth, multi-account round-robin, streaming/non-streaming/WebSocket, tools, multimodal and configurable upstreams.
items.purpose: Establish local CLI fit and documented feature surface.
items.boundary: README is a product claim; it does not establish post-stream retry safety, run governance, or terms compliance.

items.summary: Go SDK exposes Service.Run, Execute/ExecuteStream, config/auth watching, token refresh, hooks, request logger and context cancellation; management endpoints require secret and remote access flag.
items.purpose: Inspect embedding, cancellation, auth boundary and observability hooks.
supports: gateway can be embedded as a local sidecar/library
items.boundary: SDK examples do not prove a general cross-runtime scheduler or side-effect-safe fallback policy.

items.summary: Claude executor selects upstream model, translates request/response formats, applies thinking/tool/context rules, binds HTTP request to context and records upstream request/response metadata.
items.purpose: Check implementation shape for provider-specific translation and stream boundary.
items.boundary: One executor is not evidence for all providers or for cross-executor failover.

items.summary: Codex executor normalizes Responses reasoning/tool schemas, applies request thinking config, caches/replays reasoning signatures and logs upstream request/response chunks.
items.purpose: Check reasoning/tool continuity and response handling.
items.boundary: No conclusion about safety of replay after an external tool side effect.

items.summary: Stream executor buffers bootstrap frames, classifies overload before downstream commitment for transparent credential failover, and treats later terminal failures as in-stream delivery.
items.purpose: Evidence for first-byte retry boundary.
items.boundary: Observed in Codex executor; do not assume identical behavior across all provider executors.

items.summary: Registry tracks model metadata per provider/client, active client counts and quota-exceeded clients; ModelInfo includes capability/context/thinking fields.
items.purpose: Compare capability registry and quota-aware availability.
items.boundary: Only targeted source inspection; scheduler selection details were not exhaustively traced.

items.summary: Latest stable releases include v1.101.2 published 2026-09-24T00:17:20Z; v1.104.0-dev.1 is prerelease.
items.purpose: Select a stable version rather than a dev build.
items.boundary: Release listing does not define behavior.

items.summary: Tag v1.101.2 resolves to ccb327f032c69754445763dbec669a5d2517630c.
items.purpose: Pin source snapshot and staged Rust docs.
items.boundary: Does not show which components are production-default.

items.summary: Proxy CLI/config exposes unified OpenAI format, model list aliases, provider-qualified models, cost tracking and virtual-key budgets.
items.purpose: Establish local proxy usage and alias/deployment shape.
items.boundary: Feature documentation is not a test of all provider transforms.

items.summary: Fallback groups are ordered and layered by ordinary errors, content policy, and context-window; retries precede fallback; cooldown and spend-log metadata are documented.
items.purpose: Compare retry/fallback granularity and traceability.
items.boundary: No documented proof of post-first-byte stream failover or tool replay semantics.

items.summary: Routing strategies, deployment order, cooldown, strict RPM/TPM pre-call checks and Redis-shared state are documented; encrypted_content_affinity pins Responses follow-ups to the originating deployment/key.
items.purpose: Inspect load balancing, hard limits and sticky reasoning state.
items.boundary: Affinity is specific to encrypted content; it is not general session stickiness.

items.summary: Model UI/API shows public model name, underlying provider/litellm model, cost metadata and config-vs-database origin.
items.purpose: Confirm that public alias and actual deployment/provider remain distinct records.
items.boundary: Admin model management is not local run lifecycle governance.

items.summary: Rust core/gateway is staged; Python retains config, retries, routing policy, logging, callbacks, spend tracking and customer plugins until parity and production evidence.
items.purpose: Avoid treating a new Rust gateway as feature-complete replacement for Python proxy.
items.boundary: README is an implementation status note, not an independent production benchmark.

items.summary: Provider route contract separates entrypoint, transformation trait, prepare (resolve model/credentials/auth/URL) and handler (HTTP call/response transform).
items.purpose: Extract provider adapter layering reference.
items.boundary: Guide does not guarantee parity for every route/provider.

items.summary: Latest HTTP transport release is transports/v2.2.2 published 2026-09-23T05:23:40Z.
items.purpose: Fix Bifrost version/date anchor.
supports: current stable HTTP transport release at access time
items.boundary: Bifrost is multi-module; HTTP, core and plugins have separate versions.

items.summary: Annotated tag object resolves to commit fdeef8e3f31a3b18a61666ba49247d07bae3600a.
items.purpose: Pin immutable Bifrost source/docs.
items.boundary: Transport tag pins transport tree; plugin/core parity still needs version matching.

items.summary: Model Catalog discovers providers/models; explicit provider/model, governance weighted routing, proxy-provider prefixed models and final bare-model resolver are documented.
items.purpose: Compare route granularity and provider/model identity.
items.boundary: Docs do not prove side-effect-safe retry of arbitrary tool calls.

items.summary: Catalog combines provider model lists and pricing/capability data; wildcard and explicit allowlists have different semantics, with empty list deny-all.
items.purpose: Extract capability registry and allowlist behavior.
items.boundary: Catalog availability and provider list refresh behavior were not live-tested.

items.summary: Retries classify network/5xx versus per-key 429/401/402/403; key rotation and exponential backoff precede provider fallback, each fallback receiving its own retry budget; cancellation is non-retryable.
items.purpose: Compare failure classes and retry/fallback order.
items.boundary: The docs describe request semantics; tool side effects still require upper-layer policy.

items.summary: Virtual keys accept multiple provider/model/key scopes, weights, budgets, request/token rate limits and active status; env-backed provider keys are supported.
items.purpose: Compare credential and governance boundary.
items.boundary: This is gateway governance, not Host admission or run authorization.

items.summary: Hierarchical virtual-key/provider-config budgets and request/token limits are checked cumulatively; exhausted provider config is excluded while other eligible providers remain.
items.purpose: Inspect quota filtering before weighted routing.
items.boundary: No evidence here for durable accounting under network partitions.

items.summary: Background Responses created with background=true expose a provider-aware cancel endpoint.
items.purpose: Compare explicit cancellation surface.
items.boundary: Endpoint does not itself prove immediate upstream cancellation for every provider.

items.summary: Repository layout documents provider isolation queues, integration layers, plugin pre/post hooks, streaming accumulator, MCP agent loop, telemetry/logging/OTel plugins and context keys.
items.purpose: Locate implementation components before targeted source inspection.
supports: source layout and stated request flow
items.boundary: AGENTS.md is repository-provided source data, not Praxis instruction and not independently sufficient behavior proof.

items.summary: NetworkConfig defines retry/backoff, stream idle timeout, keepalive, connection and cancellation error types; request policy includes stream/cancel capabilities.
items.purpose: Check concrete network and cancellation configuration fields.
items.boundary: Schema fields do not alone show routing order or production defaults.

items.summary: Core owns provider queues, lifecycle, key selector, session affinity, tracing and plugin pipeline state; source inspection confirmed provider isolation structures.
items.purpose: Confirm queue/key/session/trace implementation boundary.
items.boundary: Targeted grep, not full control-flow audit.

items.summary: AgentModeExecutor iterates tool calls, separates auto-executable/non-auto-executable tools, validates code-mode calls and can execute eligible tools in parallel.
items.purpose: Assess tool-loop and replay boundary.
items.boundary: Does not prove idempotency or deduplication across a provider fallback.

items.summary: Accumulator stores stream state/chunks by request ID and tracks final markers; stream-sized data is kept outside the context values.
items.purpose: Compare stream bookkeeping and request-ID continuity.
items.boundary: Does not independently establish cross-provider stream failover.

items.summary: HTTP handler parses model and fallbacks, exposes provider/model and tool/reasoning/stream fields, and forwards provider response headers.
items.purpose: Check request surface and provider metadata propagation.
items.boundary: Targeted inspection; provider-specific converters were not exhaustively reviewed.
